full_judgment:
D.M. Ansaruddin, J.: This Rule obtained by the defendant on an application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure is directed against the ex-parte judgment and decree passed on 16.5.1991 by the Senior Assistant Judge, Shahjadpur Upazila, District Serajganj, in O.C. Suit No. 16 of 1990. 

 2. Opposite party Md. Mostafa Hossain @ Shahid brought on 15.5.1987 Other Class Suit No. 33 of 1987 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Upazila Shahjadpur, District Serajgonj, against the defendant petitioner Md. A. Quddus for cancellation of a deed of exchange (No. 2544) under which the plaintiff gave away some properties to the defendant in exchange for some land for which the defendant in return executed a separate deed of exchange (No.2543) simultaneously in favour of the plaintiff. In his written statement the defendant raised among others a general plea that the suit was not maintainable and an issue was framed accordingly. Both parties adduced evidence at the trial and the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit on merits as well as on a finding that the suit was not maintainable in absence of the other document (No. 2543) having been made subject matter of the suit. Against this decree the plaintiff took an appeal being Other Class Appeal No.72 of 1988. In course of the proceedings of the appeal the plaintiff appellant filed a petition praying for withdrawal of the appeal as well as the suit with liberty to sue afresh, on the grounds that due to some inadvertence some particulars were omitted in the plaint regarding the properties in dispute as well as the exchange document. The learned Judge alter hearing both sides allowed the prayer permitting the plaintiff-appellant to withdraw the appeal as well as the suit but specifically setting aside the decree impugned in the appeal. Against the appellate order of withdrawal the defendant- respondent obtained a Rule in Civil Revision No.983 of 1990. 

 3. Before, however, the defendant had obtained the above mentioned Rule, the plaintiff sped with the order of withdrawal to the trial Court and within 9 days of the order instituted fresh suit being O.C. Suit No.16 of 1990. The defendant took about 3 months to challenge the said order of withdrawal and obtain the Rule and an order slaying operation thereof. The proceedings of the O.C. suit were going on ex-parte, and it was only on 27.11.1990 that the present petitioner defendant filed a petition before the trial court praying for stay of the proceedings of the suit informing the court that he had already obtained a Rule against the appellate order of withdrawal of the earlier suit but not informing that he had already obtained the stay order although annexing with the petition an information slip issued from this Court containing such information. On the other hand, the plaintiff appeared in the revision case on 31.3.1991. Knowing fully well that the operation of the appellate order of withdrawal had been stayed by this Court he ran to the trial Court and on 6.4.1991 filed a petition praying for recording his deposition on commission. The deposition was ultimately recorded and the suit was at long last decreed ex-parte on 16.5.1991. 

 4. It has been urged by Mr. Sultan Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, that the order of stay having been passed by this Court, although during the continuance of the proceedings of the lower Court, the court below was absolutely without jurisdiction to pass the decree in the suit. Mr. Mahbuhey Alam, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, on the other hand submits that the order of stay passed by this Court was for all practical purposes infructuous as it was passed subsequent to the filing of the suit, there having been nothing to be stayed. 

 7. Mr. Alam has, however, raised a plea that the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial court cannot be set aside in revision under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure or in other words under that section there cannot be any revision against the decree as there cannot be any revision against the decree as there lies an appeal in the District Court. Such a view in my opinion is not in accordance with the provision of the said section. A party who does not prefer an appeal to the District Court is under that section at liberty to come for revision against a judgment and decree against which no appeal lies to the High Court Division. The decision reported in 42 DLR 220 may in this connection be referred to, where in it has been held that revision is barred only when there is a right of appeal in the High Court Division and not when the applicant has a right of appeal to the subordinate Court. I cannot, therefore, find my way to uphold the contention raised by Mr. Alam as to the maintainability of the revision. I must, therefore, agree with Mr. Sultan Ahmad that the ex-parte decree passed against the petitioner by the court below has been absolutely without jurisdiction. In such view of the matter, it must he held that the learned Assistant Judge, in passing the decree, has committed a serious error of law which has resulted in his decision being erroneous occasioning failure of justice. The impugned judgment and decree cannot, therefore be sustained and is liable to be set aside. 

 8. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs the impugned judgment and decree passed on 16.5.1991 by the Senior Assistant Judge Shahajadpr Upazilla, District Serajganj in O.C. Suit No.16 of set aside
